Build a simple web crawler. You get a `startUrl` and an object `htmlParser` whose method `htmlParser.getUrls(url)` returns every link found on the page at `url`. Starting from `startUrl`, follow links to discover pages, but only keep and visit pages that share the same hostname as `startUrl` (the part right after `http://`, up to the next `/`). Never fetch the same page twice. Return every page you reached, in any order.

For the examples, the pages are given as a list `urls`, and `edges[i] = [a, b]` means the page `urls[a]` links to `urls[b]`.

Example 1:

```
Input: urls = ["http://news.yahoo.com","http://news.yahoo.com/news","http://news.google.com"], edges = [[0,1],[1,2],[1,0]], startUrl = "http://news.yahoo.com"
Output: ["http://news.yahoo.com","http://news.yahoo.com/news"]
```

Example 2:

```
Input: urls = ["http://a.com","http://a.com/x","http://a.com/y"], edges = [[0,1],[1,2]], startUrl = "http://a.com"
Output: ["http://a.com","http://a.com/x","http://a.com/y"]
```

Constraints:

* `1 <= urls.length <= 1000`
* `1 <= urls[i].length <= 300`
* `startUrl` is one of the `urls`
* A hostname has only lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, and uses no trailing slash
* There are no duplicate links on the same page

Example 2:

```
Input: urls = ["http://a.com/p","http://a.com/q","http://b.com/r"], edges = [[0,1],[1,0],[0,2]], startUrl = "http://a.com/p"
```

Design a `Leaderboard` class that tracks player scores:

* `Leaderboard()` creates an empty leaderboard.
* `void addScore(playerId, score)` adds `score` to the player's running total. If the player is not on the board yet, add them with that score.
* `int top(K)` returns the sum of the `K` largest totals currently on the board.
* `void reset(playerId)` sets that player's total back to `0`, as if they had started over. The player is guaranteed to be on the board before this call.

Example 1:

```
Input: ["Leaderboard","addScore","addScore","addScore","addScore","addScore","top","reset","reset","addScore","top"]
       [[],[1,73],[2,56],[3,39],[4,51],[5,4],[1],[1],[2],[2,51],[3]]
Output: [null,null,null,null,null,null,73,null,null,null,141]
```

```
Input: ["Leaderboard","addScore","addScore","top","reset","top"]
       [[],[1,10],[2,20],[2],[2],[1]]
Output: [null,null,null,30,null,10]
```

Constraints:

* `1 <= playerId, K <= 10^4`
* `K` is at most the number of players on the board
* `1 <= score <= 100`
* At most `1000` calls are made in total
